surfaces.part: grass-to-water terrain tile, flat ground with a dark teal water region and a lighter teal shoreline edge

answer.evidence: The tile is a full 16x16 terrain autotile mask: a grass field with a dark teal water pool inside it. It is seen flat from above, with no standing volume, no front face and no edge line or eave shadow. The column scans show only color changes along the shoreline (grass, then a lighter teal edge, then dark water, then a lighter edge, then grass). These are ground-material transitions, not a top and front face. Kind is terrain, so it matches.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small ground piece, a dark teal pond with a lighter rim on olive grass. It has 7 visible tones per tile, against 3 for the reference grass and 7 for the reference paving. Near-flat coverage is 0%, the same as both references, so there are no 5x5 flat fills. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans teal/green and reads as the dark tone of the adjacent water and grass rather than a black sticker line. Shading is modest, roughly 3-4 steps per material, and the water is a fairly simple blob, so it is not as layered as the reference grass tufts. Against the grass reference it matches on visible tone count and has no flat areas. The image is tiny, so judging by eye is limited, and the measured facts carry most of this verdict. It passes narrowly.
